items.item: Data files in examples.py are plain CSV text, not Parquet — disclosed in the script's own docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1. The measured cost shapes (full-file rewrite expensive to write, read cost growing with unmerged log count, compaction resetting it) are the general mechanism every row-log-over-base design shares, not a claim of reproducing Parquet's binary layout.

The 'merge' in scan_base_with_overlay is a Python dict lookup per row, not Iceberg's real position/equality delete matching or a RoaringBitmap scan — the measured cost grows with the number of unmerged log files opened and parsed, which is the dominant, representative cost in a real system too.

examples.py's first version measured total MOR read time (base scan + merge) directly and asserted growth across rounds; this was flaky (roughly 1 in 3 runs) because the large base-scan's I/O noise swamped the real merge-overhead signal. Fixed by isolating build_overlay_from_logs (21-repeat median) from the shared scan_base_with_overlay, so the asserted signal is the isolated merge-prep cost, not total wall-clock read time.

items.item: Delta's deletion-vectors feature is documented as 'in experimental support mode' as of Delta Lake 2.3.0+, and MERGE support for deletion vectors was only added in 3.1.0 — this topic treats deletion vectors as Delta's real, documented MOR-equivalent mechanism today, not a claim it has always been Delta's default or stable-forever behavior.

This topic does not cover how a deletion vector is actually recorded on disk (the bitmap/Puffin-blob mechanism) — that is explicitly the next topic's subject, and this topic's own handoff names that boundary.
